chief_complaint: confusion, fever, and a purple rash
hpi_details: 42M brought in by his wife for acute confusion, fever, and extreme weakness over 2 days. He has a purpuric rash on his legs. Labs done in triage show severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated creatinine.

core_concepts: Classic pentad: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), thrombocytopenia, neurologic symptoms, renal failure, fever.
Caused by ADAMTS13 deficiency leading to massive microthrombi.
common_misconceptions: Waiting for all 5 symptoms of the pentad (often only MAHA and thrombocytopenia are present initially).
dangerous_errors: Transfusing platelets in TTP, which 'adds fuel to the fire' and worsens thrombosis.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 42M presenting with acute encephalopathy, fever, and purpura.
reference_soap.objective: Confused. Petechiae/purpura. Labs: Hgb 7.0, Platelets 15k, Cr 2.2, Schistocytes on smear.
reference_soap.plan: STAT Hematology consult for emergency Plasma Exchange. DO NOT transfuse platelets.

learning_objectives: Recognize the deadly presentation of TTP and the contraindication to platelet transfusion.

teaching.one_liner: Acute presentation of MAHA, thrombocytopenia, and neurologic changes requiring emergency plasma exchange.

must_ask.say: When did the confusion start, and how has it changed over the past day?
Where did the purple rash appear first, and has it been spreading?
How high has your fever been, and when did it start?
Have you noticed any change in how much urine you are passing, or its color?
Have you had any recent bloody diarrhea or infection?

history.answer: My wife brought me in because I've had a fever, I feel completely out of it and confused, and these purple spots appeared on my legs.
The fever and weakness started about two days ago, and I have felt progressively worse since then.
My temperature reached around 38.3 degrees at home with shaking chills, and the heat feels constant rather than coming and going.
My wife gave me two acetaminophen pills yesterday, but my fever barely came down and my head stayed foggy.
I began feeling muddled and forgetting things yesterday morning, and my wife says I've been drifting in and out of confusion.
I have a dull, generalized headache, but my neck does not feel stiff or painful when I move it.
These dark purple spots and patches showed up on both of my shins yesterday, and they do not fade when pressed.
My gums bled a bit when I brushed yesterday morning, but I haven't had nosebleeds, black stools, or blood in my phlegm.
I have barely produced any urine today, and the little bit that came out looked very dark, almost like tea.
No, I haven't had any stomach bug, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea at all before this started.
I feel sick to my stomach from being so weak, but I don't have belly pain or vomiting.
I don't have any cough, phlegm, sore throat, or trouble catching my breath.
There is no burning or pain when I pass urine, and my lower back and sides don't hurt.
I haven't noticed any tick or insect bites, there are no dark crusts on my skin, and my joints don't ache.
No drenching night sweats and no unexplained weight loss before these past two days.
I haven't felt any swollen glands or lumps in my neck, armpits, or groin.
I haven't traveled outside the city, gone hiking in tall grass, or handled farm animals recently.
Nobody in my family, household, or office has been sick with anything like this.
No, I've never received chemotherapy, cortisone steroids, or any immune-suppressing drugs.
I don't have any heart valve problems or heart disease, and I haven't had any dental work done recently.
I haven't started taking any new prescription pills, over-the-counter drugs, or health tonics.
I have been married for fifteen years with no other sexual partners, and I have never used intravenous or recreational drugs.
My wife is terrified that I might have meningitis because of my fever, confusion, and the rash.
I feel so exhausted and disoriented that I'm truly terrified something fatal is happening to me.
We need you to figure out what is wrong right away and transfer me to the intensive care unit if necessary.
I have always been completely healthy with no high blood pressure, diabetes, or kidney trouble.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital before.
I do not take any daily medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products in my life.
I might have a single glass of beer on a weekend gathering, but I don't drink regularly.
I work as an office accountant at a commercial firm and live in an apartment with my wife.
No one in my family has a history of blood disorders, bleeding tendencies, kidney failure, or autoimmune diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 106 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, body temperature 38.3 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Appears acutely ill, markedly pale, fatigued, and noticeably confused.
Fluctuating attention, disoriented to day and date, with slow cognitive processing.
Prominent conjunctival pallor and mild scleral icterus present.
Pale oral mucosa with trace dried blood along the gingival line, but posterior pharynx is clear without erythema or exudate.
No cervical lymphadenopathy palpable in anterior or posterior chains.
Full passive cervical range of motion without neck stiffness; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation without wheezes, rhonchi, or crackles.
Tachycardic regular rhythm with normal S1 and S2; faint grade II systolic flow murmur without rubs or gallops.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, non-distended, with no guarding, rebound, or palpable organomegaly.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on percussion bilaterally.
Multiple non-blanching petechiae and purple purpuric macules scattered over both lower legs, with no eschar or ulceration.
